shortDescription: Brazil's Congress on Tuesday approved a bill exempting data-center-related equipment from federal taxes, part of the government's plan to lure such projects to the country.

children: Brazil's Congress on Tuesday approved a bill exempting data-center-related equipment from federal taxes, part of the government's plan to lure such projects to the country.
The Senate approved the bill on Tuesday, following a previous greenlight from the lower house; the text now heads to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva for ratification
The bill exempts key federal taxes - PIS, Cofins, IPI, and import duties - on IT-related capital expenditures for the sector, such as on servers and refrigeration
The government issued an executive order on the matter in 2025, but the proposal expired this year after it was not voted on by Congress
The text approved on Tuesday is a similar bill, proposed this year by the then government leader in the lower house Jose Guimaraes, now the minister for institutional relations

title: Brazil's Congress approves tax exemptions to attract data center investments
